title: Air Assist Pressure Knob Not Responding
body_html:
Air Assist Pressure Value Remains Unchanged When Turning the Knob

This guide explains why the Air Assist pressure may remain static despite adjusting the knob and pressing the "Test" button, and provides step-by-step troubleshooting methods to restore proper pressure control.

Problem Description

  • When pressing the "Test" button, the inlet pressure value displayed on the digital gauge remains identical to the idle value (before pressing the button). Turning the adjustment knob does not change the live reading, and the value stays locked at the initial pressure.
  • Only after releasing the button does the pressure reading slowly drift toward the newly adjusted setting, taking 3 to 5 minutes to finally stabilize.

Cause

  • Air Source Issues: An incorrect setting or limitation on the air supply itself (air pump or air compressor).
  • Pneumatic Leak: A leak or loose connection anywhere along the air lines.
  • Gauge Lockout: The digital gauge is stuck in lock mode, which can cause reading and refresh anomalies.
  • Restricted Valve: An internal air pipe valve is overtightened, choking off the airflow entirely.
  • Hardware Fault: Internal component damage inside the Air Assist Kit itself.

Solution

Method 1. Inspect the Air Source and Tubing

Check the built-in air pump (for X Series) or your external air compressor to ensure they are powered on and delivering adequate pressure.

Inspect the external air lines feeding into the Air Assist Kit. Ensure all push-to-connect fittings are seated firmly and check the tubing for punctures, crimps, or leaks.

Method 2. Unlock and Reset the Digital Gauge (If Locked)

If you notice a key icon on the left side of the digital display, it is locked. Press and hold both the "S" and "▼" buttons simultaneously. After a few seconds, the main screen will display "Lock" and the sub-screen will read "OFF", indicating a successful unlock.

Disconnect the main air supply line. Press and hold both the "▲" and "▼" buttons until the displayed reading returns to exactly 0. Reconnect the air source, press the "Test" button, and turn the knob to check if it now regulates properly.

Method 3. Inspect Internal Air Valves

Hydra Gen1 Series

Locate the air pipe needle valve on the back of the X-axis guide rail. Check if the needle valve has been turned completely tight, choking the airflow. While maintaining safety, place a tissue beneath the laser nozzle to feel for air output while turning the needle valve. Adjust it until you feel a steady stream of air and the Air Assist Kit gauge begins to update fluidly.

X Series

Remove the laser head cover to expose the valve connected to the end of the internal air tubing. Please refer to this guide for step-by-step adjustment instructions: How to Adjust the Air Pipe Screw

 ⚠️ Important Note

If none of the methods above resolve the issue, it is likely that an internal component within the Air Assist Kit is defective. Please document your troubleshooting results and contact ONELASER After-Sales Support for assistance with a replacement part.

 

Important Reminder:

If these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
